clue.text: Labour's last tv correspondent — just about nothing on — a big turn-off for audiences?

indicators.note: the final letter of Labour is the one wanted

parts.note: its final letter is taken

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next pieces sit inside the reporter's name

parts.note: Kate Adie, the BBC's famous chief news correspondent of the 1990s
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Labour-supporting television reporter appears virtually naked, which viewers find no thrill at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Kate Adie with nothing on. 'last' picks R from Labour; 'just about' wraps her name round O and ON, making ADIOONE. Radio One is the BBC's pop station, mocked as what listeners switch off.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a joke: the station is something listeners are imagined switching off, a dig at its programming.

clue.text: See 23
Hey, Pam, time to jiggle, giving good vibrations!

indicators.note: jiggling shakes things about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone urges Pam to start dancing so that the mood becomes lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to jiggle' looks like an instruction to Pam to dance, but it is the signal to shake the letters up. Good vibrations here are fellow feeling between people, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is sharing another person's feelings, which loosely gives the friendly rapport called good vibes.

clue.text: Dead wood — ends up a politician,…

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what is left of a felled tree
second meaning: to tour making campaign speeches, as someone does who ends up in politics

explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs on into 5 down; read alone it gives two senses of one word, the leftover base of a tree and the verb for political campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tree's dead base and campaigning by speechmaking, as in being on the campaign trail.

clue.text: … pisspoor PM, first class dolt of an ambassador

indicators.note: something pisspoor is botched or badly done, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first class, written here with the letter I standing in for the numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: A useless Prime Minister and a top-rank idiot serving as an envoy abroad are mocked together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pisspoor' rearranges PM, AI and DOLT. The clue runs on from 4 down in the surface. A1 for first class is shown with I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representing his country abroad, of whom an ambassador is the senior example.

clue.text: It's definitely the main Indian dish around

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan, a British-Indian dish
C, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a particular curry is by far the best Indian food going.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea; 'definitely' points to the definite article: this sea is always called THE Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is a northern European sea, always named with the definite article, and the main is a poetic word for sea.

clue.text: See 12
Brenda, Brian, relatively speaking, joined a member of society

parts.note: Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; she is Charles's mother, so MA
Private Eye calls Prince Charles Brian; as family he is the Queen's son

explanation.surface: Two people named Brenda and Brian, related in some way, sign up to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye gave the royals nicknames: Brenda for the Queen and Brian for Prince Charles, so in family terms they are mother and son.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason, or Freemason, belongs to a secretive fraternal society with its own lodges and rites.

clue.text: A Tory government scandal when members on a riot interfered with Queen

parts.note: arms are limbs, members of the body

indicators.note: letters that are interfered with are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A government scandal breaks after rioting MPs disturb the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interfered with' gives TOIRA. Arms to Iraq was the 1990s affair over British firms selling military equipment to Saddam Hussein, investigated by the Scott Inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: The affair over weapons-related exports to Iraq embarrassed John Major's Conservative ministers, making it a scandal of that administration.

clue.text: School's after equipment — cheap and vulgar stuff!

indicators.note: the school abbreviation comes after the equipment word

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school buying kit ends up with tacky, tasteless goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art or decoration in poor taste, gaudy and sentimental, which matches cheap vulgar stuff.

clue.text: Terrorist weapon gets Bough fired up, so it's said

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud to give the sound of the answer

parts.note: a bough is an arm of a tree, and fired up is alight, so ARM ALIGHT

explanation.surface: A terrorist weapon sets the TV presenter Frank Bough ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so it's said' means ARM ALIGHT is spoken to give the weapon. Frank Bough was a BBC presenter brought down by a 1980s scandal; here his name is just a tree branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armalite rifle was notoriously the gun of the IRA during the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Lots of muck-raking here, in the Eye

definitions.text: Lots of muck-raking here, in the Eye

parts.words: Lots of muck-raking here, in the Eye
parts.note: plenty of literal raking of manure goes on in this rural setting, and the phrase is a Private Eye section heading for countryside stories

explanation.walkthrough: Muck-raking suggests the scandal-digging the Eye is famous for, but read literally it is a farmyard chore; the Eye runs a farming column under this heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard is where manure is literally raked up, and Private Eye uses the phrase as a regular agricultural column title.

clue.text: Liberal parents don't do this sort of heroin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hit a child as punishment, which permissive parents avoid
second meaning: a slang name for heroin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface links permissive parenting with drugs, but the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for slapping a child and the street-drug slang term for heroin.

clue.text: Labour, for this sort of mother, benefits someone else

definitions.text: Labour, for this sort of mother, benefits someone else

parts.words: Labour, for this sort of mother, benefits someone else
parts.note: the labour is childbirth, and a mother who carries a baby for another couple gives birth on their behalf

explanation.walkthrough: Labour wants to be the political party, as 'benefits' suggests welfare; it is in fact giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate mother bears a child for another person, so her labour of childbirth is done for someone else.

clue.text: Blimey! Long tv show needed to get one to shut up a politician …!

definitions.text: one to shut up a politician

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of surprise, like blimey
ER was the long-running American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An exasperated viewer wishes a lengthy television programme would silence a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler interrupts a speaker with shouted taunts, trying to drown out or silence someone addressing a meeting.

clue.text: Roger gets up to a prank — Viz-type humour?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to roger is slang for having sex, as is to bonk
a prank is a practical joke

explanation.surface: Someone named Roger gets out of bed to play a practical trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' reads BONK upwards as KNOB. Viz is a British adult comic famous for crude humour, and knob is British slang for penis.
explanation.definitionFit: Viz traded heavily in crude genital gags, which is exactly the schoolboy smut the phrase names.

clue.text: … only Frost for recompense

parts.note: just means only, merely
ice is frozen water, like frost

explanation.surface: Continuing 15, it suggests only the interviewer David Frost could make amends for the politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the broadcaster David Frost from 15's television theme; it is just frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is fair treatment of wrongs, which includes redress or due reward for an injury done.

clue.text: Newt's lot: bonking!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the US ..., led by Speaker Newt Gingrich in the mid-1990s
second meaning: sexual intercourse, an old formal sense of the word

explanation.walkthrough: Newt suggests the amphibian; it is Newt Gingrich, the Republican Speaker of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the American legislature Gingrich led and, in a dated sense, sexual union.

clue.text: What makes Boris pass out over Channel…?

indicators.note: the channel's name goes outside and over the other word, holding it within

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite television channel
taken as written

explanation.surface: It asks what drink makes Boris Yeltsin collapse while flying over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris suggests Yeltsin, notorious for drinking; the answer completes the name of Boris Spassky, the Soviet world chess champion. 'out over' signals that the channel's name encloses the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spassky is the surname that turns the bare forename into the full name of the famous Russian chess grandmaster.

clue.text: On date, poor circulation makes you lose an erection

indicators.note: circulating sends letters round, so the word poor is rearranged

explanation.surface: On a date, bad blood flow leaves a man unable to stay aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' sends the letters round to give ROOP; 'poor circulation' reads as a medical complaint, which suits the surface nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or go limp, which is what happens when an erection is lost.

clue.text: … Russia's ready to get Tory leader out of difficulty

indicators.note: the Tory leader's letter is taken out of the word for difficulty

parts.note: trouble means difficulty

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of Tory is meant

parts.note: its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Russia is willing to help a Conservative chief escape from his problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks the first letter of Tory, and 'out of' removes it. Ready is British slang for cash, as in 'the ready', so Russia's ready is its currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is Russia's unit of money, and ready money is slang for cash.

clue.text: The tosser's deposit holding institution?

parts.note: a tosser is crude British slang for a masturbator, and his deposit is semen, held at a clinic for donors

explanation.walkthrough: Deposit and institution suggest an ordinary bank; the depositor is a donor of semen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm bank stores donated semen for fertility treatment, so it literally holds such deposits like a bank.

clue.text: Shadow minister's brain screwed up in the morning by a nag's outburst, we hear

indicators.note: screwing up something crumples it, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: M is short for morning, as in a.m.

indicators.note: the horse's noise is spoken, giving the sound of the last part

parts.note: a nag is a horse, whose outburst is a whinny

explanation.surface: A shadow minister's thinking is ruined one morning by someone's nagging tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screwed up' jumbles the first name; 'we hear' gives WHINNEY by sound. Brian Mawhinney, Tory party chairman, became shadow Home Secretary after Labour won in 1997. The nag is a horse, not a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: After the 1997 election Mawhinney sat on the Tory front bench in opposition, a shadow cabinet member.

clue.text: Second Conservative horny beast to piss off!

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep with horns

explanation.surface: A second randy Tory is told to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a brusque order to leave at once, the same as the vulgar command to go away.

clue.text: They get talked about, Brenda's people!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Queen's citizens; Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen

explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, so her people are those she reigns over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both topics discussed in conversation and the people living under a monarch's rule.

clue.text: Clinton's vice: squeezing the thing to produce an abnormal swelling!

indicators.note: squeezing holds one piece tightly within another

parts.note: Al Gore was Bill Clinton's Vice President
it means the thing

explanation.surface: It hints at a sexual vice of President Clinton producing an unwanted swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' signals one piece held inside another. Vice wants to be a moral failing given Clinton's reputation; it is his vice president.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, seen as a swelling in the neck.

clue.text: Much criticism associated with skin protection often seen on Kate's chest

parts.note: flak is heavy hostile criticism
a jacket is a protective outer covering, as the skin of a potato is

explanation.surface: A sunscreen product attracts criticism despite often being worn on a woman's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Kate Adie, the BBC war correspondent who reported from battle zones wearing body armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A flak jacket is bulletproof body armour, the vest war reporter Kate Adie was regularly filmed in.

clue.text: US agency that sends up people

definitions.text: US agency that sends up people

parts.words: US agency that sends up people
parts.note: sending up suggests mocking, but this American body literally launches astronauts into space

explanation.walkthrough: To send up is British slang for to mock, which fits a satirical magazine; here it means launch into orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: The American space agency launches crewed missions, lifting astronauts into space.
